title: Relay App Alternatives: Best Options for 2026
summary: Relay app alternatives differ based on the reason your team is leaving. Identify which option solves your actual problem.
body_markdown:
## Build the Same Workflow in Activepieces


You can rebuild a Relay.app-style workflow in Activepieces with the same shape: a trigger, an AI step, a write to your tools.


It fits best if your reason for leaving is open source (the core is MIT-licensed), self-hosting, or wanting an AI step that works across many apps.


The test is the same one: move one workflow, not all of them.


Start with the plainest prompt, because it shows quickly whether the AI step is doing real work: "Pull the vendor, amount, date and category out of this expense submission."


In Activepieces that's a single step that returns named fields, not a paragraph you have to parse, and the free plan ($0, 1,000 credits a month) allows unlimited flows, so you can keep a separate flow for each prompt variation you try.


For a reimbursement tracker, the flow below does exactly that. A web form starts it, the second step (selected) extracts the structured fields, a Google Sheets step inserts the row, and an AI step follows.


On the right, the panel gives you a published form URL and a draft one, plus a test trigger that generates sample data. So you can check the extraction against a real submission before anything touches your spreadsheet.


Next to the screenshot is the part to check on your own account: whether each step runs against the apps you actually use.


### What maps across from Relay


Everything maps across directly: triggers, app actions and AI steps. Each app connection is called a piece, so the first check is whether the apps your workflow touches appear in the[piece list](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) .


If one is missing, you'll find out in ten minutes, not after a migration. That matters most if app coverage was why you left.


Nothing confines the AI step to one app. It can read from a form, a spreadsheet or a message and hand the result to any later step, which is what makes the reimbursement flow above possible without glue code.


If you want to try it, you can[sign up free](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Frelay-app-alternatives-best-options-for-2026) and rebuild your chosen workflow there.


On pricing, I won't quote a number I can't point at. Open the pricing page and check how runs, steps and any usage limits are counted for your plan, then multiply by your workflow's real step count.


If per-step cost was your reason for leaving, that arithmetic is the whole test.


### Approval and self-hosting


Because Activepieces' core is MIT-licensed, you can run it on your own infrastructure, which means workflow data stays in an environment you control. The enterprise directories (` packages/ee/` ) sit under a separate commercial licence, so check which features you need.


That's the direct answer if hosting was your reason for leaving.


The trade is that you now maintain it: updates, backups and uptime become your job.


For approvals, the same web form trigger in the screenshot is a human input step, so a person can be put in front of an action before it happens.


Build that into your test workflow on purpose: route the extracted row to a reviewer first, and see whether the pause behaves the way your team needs.


Then check the pricing page for any limits on self-hosted versus cloud features before you commit.
